subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class localhost plus Telegram owner bootstrap surface, and should it live in non-interactive onboarding, a dedicated bootstrap command, or plugin-owned setup hooks?
rationale: The item is useful and vision-aligned, but it changes how setup exposes security decisions across Gateway auth, Telegram bot credentials, and DM owner authorization.

options.title: Design a first-class bootstrap
options.body: Add a supported bootstrap surface only after maintainers choose the command boundary, owner-preapproval model, and token/SecretRef handling.

options.title: Narrow to Telegram owner setup
options.body: Keep daemon and dashboard commands separate and solve only Telegram numeric owner allowlist or resolver automation first.

options.title: Document manual composition
options.body: Leave core behavior as separate commands and document a secure scripted sequence using existing onboarding, dashboard, and channels commands.

recommendation.title: Design a first-class bootstrap
recommendation.body: Add a supported bootstrap surface only after maintainers choose the command boundary, owner-preapproval model, and token/SecretRef handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily affects setup/onboarding product shape, with Telegram and dashboard owners involved for implementation details.
